entries.build_command: make -j$(nproc) TARGET=linux-glibc USE_OPENSSL=1 USE_QUIC=1 USE_QUIC_OPENSSL_COMPAT=1 USE_LUA=1 USE_PCRE2=1 ARCH_FLAGS='-O0 -g --coverage' LDFLAGS='--coverage'
entries.reachability_signal: gcov on src/quic_tx.c showing coverage of lines 2041 (added len -= len_sz_diff)
entries.expected_signal: haproxy -c returns exit code 0 for valid QUIC config; gcov shows changed lines executed when QUIC Initial packet is built
entries.input_strategy: Build haproxy with QUIC support. Create a minimal config with a QUIC (HTTP/3) frontend listener. Validate config parsing via -c flag. For runtime packet building: run haproxy as daemon, connect with a QUIC client (e.g. ngtcp2-client or quic-client) to trigger Initial packet exchange, send SIGTERM, collect gcov data.
entries.limitations: 1) vtest/varnishtest not installed, so QUIC reg-tests cannot run. 2) No QUIC client tool (ngtcp2, quiche, aioquic) available for runtime packet-level testing. 3) Runtime QUIC packet building probe requires external QUIC client and root/loopback setup. 4) OpenSSL headers 3.0.18 vs runtime 3.0.13 - do not use for cryptographic compatibility conclusions. 5) Coverage instrumentation (-O0 -g --coverage) may not produce identical binaries to production builds.
